texts.preamble: M/S Bengal Sweets vs Venkatesh S on 29 March, 2025 1 Os 1694/2022 Kabc010070202022 In The Court Of Xv Additonal City Civil & Sessions: Judge At Bengaluru (Cch.No.3) Dated this 29th day of March 2025 O.S. No. 1694/2022 Present :- Sri. Laxman.Ramu.Kurane,B.Com, Llm Xv Additional City Civil & Sessions Judge, Bengaluru. Plaintiff/s :- M/s. Bengal Sweets A Sweet Meat Stall at Shop No. 160/D Gangamma Circle Jalahalli Bengaluru-560 013. Represented by its proprietor Mr. Bipul Dolui (Rep.by Sri. Gm, Advocate) V/s Defendant/s :- 1. Shri S. Venkatesh
texts.facts: 2. The brief facts of the plaintiff's case is as under :- The plaintiff is the Proprietor of M/s. Bengal Sweets and it is running its business in the suit schedule property from past 31 years by obtaining registration certificate from the Department of Labour and the same is valid till 31.12.2023. The plaintiff also obtained trade license from the Health Department and also obtained the license under Food and Safety Standards Authority of India. The plaintiff is known to be one M/S Bengal Sweets vs Venkatesh S on 29 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/156999067/ 2 of the best Sweet Stall in the locality and as customers coming around from all corners of Bangalore to enjoy the delicious sweets. The defendant No.1 in the month of May 2021 approached the plaintiff claiming to be President of Dalitha Yuvakara Sevadala and demanded sum of Rs 10,00,000/- to permit the plaintiff to continue running the business. The plaintiff stated that he is running the business in compliance of all local laws and did not find a reason to pay the ransom as demanded by the Defendant No.1. The plaintiff stated that the defendant No.1 again sent Defendants 2 to 4 to the shop on 16.11.2021 holding out a threat that they would shut the shop unless he pays a sum of Rs 10,00,000/-. The defendant No.5 claiming to be from the News Alert 24 x 7 barged into the shop and making videos of the shop and kitchen wherein sweets were being prepared. The plaintiff requested the defendant No.5 to show his identity card and he refused to pay any heed and started holding an interview of the henchmen of some paid up men who are not customers of the shop. The plaintiff submitted that the defendants after leaving the premises yet again over the telephone called for an oral settlement and held the same offer and any failure to comply with the offer, they would screen the doctored images of the kitchen in the press and news channels, ruin the reputation and get the shop permanently shut down. Hence the present suit. 3. The defendants 1 to 4 after service of summons neither appeared nor contested the suit of the plaintiff. The defendant No.5 after service of summons appeared through his counsel and filed Written Statement contending that that the defendants 1 to 4 are the local people, regular customer to the plaintiff and they have advised the plaintiff to make clean and maintain hygienic in the place of preparing foods and sweets. But the plaintiff failed to keep up the promise. The defendant No.5 submitted that he made oral complaint to the concerned Department to take necessary action against the plaintiff and it was came to the knowledge of the defendants that the officials also hand in glove with the plaintiff and not taken any action against the plaintiff. The defendants have made inspection of the premises of sweet preparation place, made photograph, taken photos for the purpose of submitting before concerned Department. The defendant filed a complaint to the Commissioner for Food and Health Controller on 18.2.2022 and also filed complaint before jurisdictional police on 6.2.2022 against the plaintiff. The defendants 1 to 4 have made the complaint, sought action from the concerned Department. Since no action taken from the Departments, the defendants with the social obligations for the public and the locality has taken protest and requested the plaintiff to keep up cleanness and hygienic of the place where food is prepared and except this the defendants have no interest in the business of the plaintiff. Accordingly prays to dismiss the suit with exemplary cost. The plaintiff in order to prove his case against the defendants got examined its Proprietor as P.W.1 and got marked Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10 documents. The plaintiff submitted that he is running the business in compliance of all local laws and did not find a reason to pay the ransom as demanded by the Defendant No.1.
